title: Splicing a segment of a computation
statement: Let $M$ be a nondeterministic machine with $k$ work tapes, Boolean input $x$, state set $S$, and configuration $c$ on $x$. Let $w$ be a finite choice word and let $a,b$ be natural numbers with $a\le b\le |w|$. Suppose that the configurations reached after the first $a$ and first $b$ choices have the same core data and the same output summary. If the middle segment of choices from positions $a$ through $b$ is deleted, the resulting run has the same core data and output summary as the run under all of $w$. Moreover, every prefix of the shortened choice word has the same core data and output summary as some prefix of $w$, whose length is at most $|w|$.
